entries.suspected: assign_items (match.py:53-81) computes a full item-to-track cost matrix from track_distance and hands it to lap.lapjv, which always returns a complete minimum-cost mapping; it never rejects a pair, however costly, and never leaves an item and a track both unmatched when the counts agree. This item set carries the same title ("Session Tape") on every item, matching the release's own "Session Tape A/B/C" tracks with an identical string_dist value (0.083333) regardless of which track it is paired against -- proven, not merely asserted, by the record's own per-track cost matrix -- so title is mathematically incapable of discriminating a correct pairing from a wrong one, and length is the only signal the solver has left. Item 0's length (222s) sits within track_length_grace (10s) of track 1's length (230s) but 12s outside grace of its own true track 0 (200s); item 1 (208s) is the mirror image. lap.lapjv's own optimum is therefore assignment {0:1, 1:0, 2:2}: items 0 and 1 swapped, item 2 correct. That optimum costs 0.15 total (album distance 0.016667, strong, apply); the correct pairing {0:0, 1:1, 2:2} would have cost 0.47 (album distance 0.052222, medium) had the solver ever considered rejecting the cheaper wrong one, which it structurally cannot.
